title: Redwood June 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company-wide all-hands. CEO opens with Q2 results and org updates, CTO/Head of Product present technical and product progress (Dedicated, Private, runtime perf), security gives compliance update, sales shares GTM highlights and upcoming enterprise pilots. Ends with Q&A and recap of next steps.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Slides: https://redwood.com/slides/june-2026-allhands (internal)
Attendees: Elena Park, Ravi Singh, Priya Kapoor, Marcus Wu, Sofia Alvarez, Morgan Lee, Drew Chen, Lina Torres + All Staff

Summary (auto): Q2 execution beat plan on revenue and efficiency, Dedicated adoption growth, early Private pilots signed, continued improvement in token-level costs from runtime optimizations.

[00:00] Elena Park: Hey everyone, welcome to the June all-hands. Uh, quick note, we'll run about an hour, stick to questions at the end. I want to start with a quick Q2 update.
[00:22] Elena Park: So high level, revenue was up, ARR grew 14% quarter over quarter, we shipped Dedicated GA to two new customers, and Private pilots are now in three regulated accounts. Folks, that is huge, like, really great work across the board.
[00:48] Marcus Wu: (muted) yeah huge props to infra and runtime teams, batching and kv cache changes dropped median latency by ~12% on common workloads, rough numbers in the deck.
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: On product, we shipped model catalog improvements, function/tool calling for hosted API, and added per-route tracing in the console. A reminder: the rollout for the new caching defaults goes live in two weeks, see the RFC.
[01:33] Ravi Singh: I want to call out an important caveat while we reduced latency, tail latency for long context still needs work. We're experimenting with sequence-aware kernel selection; early lab results look promising but not yet production ready.
[01:58] Elena Park: Great. Questions on product?
[02:05] (silence)
[02:15] Sofia Alvarez: Quick GTM note we closed two mid-market accounts on Dedicated, one was an education SaaS that wanted predictable throughput; Sales leaned on our Dedicated SLA and cost model. We're also seeing more inbound for Private, often from regulated finance and healthcare.
[02:40] Lina Torres: On customer success, pilots for Private are going well, a couple integration gotchas (SAML mapping with some customer IdPs) but workaround documented. We'll share postmortem notes.
[03:01] Elena Park: Security update?
[03:05] Drew Chen: Security: SOC 2 Type II timeline still on track, control evidence collection is ongoing, KMS/HSM integrations testing continues. A note: audit logs ingestion for Private deployments required minor schema changes engineering has a patch.
[03:28] Ravi Singh: Also adding encryption-at-rest for cache artifacts in Private low risk but helpful for compliance.
[03:40] Elena Park: Hiring/org changes Morgan?
[03:44] Morgan Lee: We're opening 18 roles in the next quarter across engineering and product; we'll run a hiring push and more referral bonuses. Also, we're reorganizing the infra team into runtime and orchestration pods to accelerate Dedicated feature work.
[04:00] Elena Park: Okay roadmap: Q3 focus is on latency & cost improvements, Private GA for two regions, more Dedicated capacity options, and launching the first Optimize recommendations in console.
[04:20] (slide change)
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: Live demo: new per-route dashboards and rollout canary controls. (demo audio) Note: demo had a small hiccup our staging console had a rate-limit bug, we recovered and demoed the rollback flow.
[04:55] Audience question (Sam J.): Can you clarify the pricing model changes for Dedicated?
[05:05] Sofia Alvarez: Yes pricing for Dedicated will have two tiers: reserved baseline + burst credits. We'll publish the pricing doc and an example TCO spreadsheet next week. Link will be posted in #all-hands.
[05:25] Audience question (Kate R.): For Private, what data residency options are available?
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: Private supports region pinning for control plane, and we have plans to support on-prem bundles for air-gapped deployments; you'll see a pilot offer for EU-based financial customers.
[05:50] Audience question (Engineer): Any updates on the model catalog and our default models?
[05:58] Ravi Singh: We're curating a set of verified open models with performance profiles. We plan to surface quantization recommendations per-model in the catalog to reduce memory and cost.
[06:15] (crosstalk)
[06:30] Drew Chen: Security question will customers be able to bring their own KMS? Yes, BYOK via supported KMS providers is in scope; for Private we've tested with AWS KMS and HashiCorp Vault.
[06:50] Elena Park: Alright let's go to the performance slide Marcus?
[06:55] Marcus Wu: Benchmarks in the deck: on G4dn-like infra, median token-latency improved ~12%, throughput for batching increased by 22% with continuous batching. Caveat: numbers vary by model architecture, sequence lengths used in customer workloads differ. Full benchmark spreadsheet will be posted.
[07:25] Priya Kapoor: We ran a cost-vs-latency analysis and are building Optimize suggestions that will recommend batching and quantization profiles based on observed traffic. Early experiments show ~30% unit-cost reduction for embeddings workloads when using newer quantized kernels.
[07:50] Audience: (murmurs)
[08:05] Elena Park: Competitors quick note, we watch OpenAI, Anthropic, Google for API features, and Databricks for managed infra; our differentiation remains prediction economics and unified tooling.
[08:28] Elena Park: Ok HR and culture Morgan?
[08:30] Morgan Lee: Parental leave policy updated, new manager training rolled out, and all-hands cadence will stay monthly. We're launching mentorship circles next month; sign-ups in the People channel.
[08:55] Q&A rapid fire:
[09:00] Question (Ishaan): Any updates to SDKs?
[09:05] Priya Kapoor: SDKs will include streaming improvements and an improved Python async client. We'll ship beta next sprint.
[09:18] Question (Sarah): Can we get more internal docs on how to interpret per-route dashboards?
[09:25] Lina Torres: We'll publish a how-to and a recorded walkthrough, link in the all-hands notes.
[09:38] (overlap)
[09:45] Elena Park: Closing notes: big thanks, keep shipping, send feedback. Recap of next steps in the chat.
[09:58] (end)
